summary: Recent technology developments highlight advancing open-source AI models, escalating cybersecurity threats driven by autonomous agents, and significant milestones in developer tooling.

items.title: Hackers hit AI coding tool OpenCode, running up charges on users’ AI accounts
items.summary: Hackers breached part of OpenCode's online platform to steal user API keys and run up unauthorized charges on connected AI accounts. The incident underscores security vulnerabilities in developer platforms, especially when automated AI tools fail to analyze malicious code during incidents.

items.title: Nvidia launches new open models to run agents in the enterprise and on PCs
items.summary: Nvidia released new open models designed to execute AI agents locally on personal computers and within enterprise data centers. The launch caters to growing demand among organizations seeking to deploy private, self-hosted AI models securely.

items.title: ReactOS reaches major milestone with NTFS install support
items.summary: ReactOS has achieved a major development milestone by integrating installation support for the NTFS file system using a new driver. This update represents significant progress in storage compatibility for the open-source operating system project.

items.title: Anthropic gives outside AI watchdog “employee-like” access
items.summary: Anthropic granted an independent watchdog internal access to evaluate its AI development and operations. The partner organization holds permission to publish its evaluation results publicly without seeking approval from Anthropic.

items.title: A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents
items.summary: An attacker deployed autonomous AI agents to breach over 100 websites, affecting major companies such as John Deere and SharkNinja. The security findings highlight expanding risks as bad actors increasingly weaponize automated AI agents to execute large-scale intrusions.
